Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate
Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J.
1.
List revised.
None appears on behalf of the applicant.

2. Heard learned AGA for the State-respondent and perused the record.
3.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant for quashing the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 172 of 04 of 2011, including the summoning order dated 10.01.2011 passed by the court below, under Sections 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Police Station concerned, District Jhansi.

4. From perusal of the record, it appears that on 24.04.2010, opposite party no. 2 conducted a raid at the shop of the applicant and purchased 20 packets (each of 750 ml) of Frootola Mango Drink upon payment.
A receipt was prepared and Form VI was duly filled at the spot.

The sample was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst, U.P., Lucknow on the same day, and the analysis report dated Ankush Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188540537/
1 15.06.2010 declared the sample as adulterated.

entities.text: Ankush Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on this report, opposite party no. 2 submitted an application before the District Magistrate, Jhansi on 16.07.2010, seeking permission to prosecute the applicant.

The said permission was granted on 10.12.2010, and consequently, Complaint Case No. 172 of 04 of 2011 under Sections 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was filed before the concerned Magistrate, who took cognizance of the offence on 10.01.2011.
The record further reveals that the applicant had preferred Criminal Revision No. 44 of 2011 before the Sessions Judge, Jhansi, challenging the summoning order, which was dismissed.

The present application has been filed seeking quashing of the complaint proceedings and the summoning order, primarily on the ground that the sanction for prosecution was granted mechanically and that the mandatory procedure under the Act was not duly followed.
5. Learned A.G.A. submits that due process was followed while collecting the sample, and there is no procedural irregularity.
The court below has rightly taken cognizance against the applicant, and no interference is required in the ongoing proceedings.
6. . Heard learned counsel for the parties.

7. From perusal of the record, this Court finds no procedural irregularity or legal infirmity in the collection of the sample, its analysis, the sanction for prosecution, or the cognizance order passed by the court below.
8. It is well settled that power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. should be exercised sparingly and only when a clear abuse of process of law or miscarriage of justice is evident.
In the present case, no such ground is made out.
The complaint, sanction, and cognizance order appear to be in accordance with law.
9.. In view of the above, the Court finds no merit in the application.
The instant application is accordingly dismissed.

Order Date :- 24.7.2025 pks  Ankush Kumar Gupta vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188540537/
